title: Normalization geonormal insep
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a finite type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. There exists a finite purely inseparable extension $k\subseteq k'$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] such that the normalization $N$ of $X_{k'}=X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is geometrically normal over $k'$: for every extension field $L/k'$, every local ring of $N_L$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Here normalization means the disjoint union of the normalizations [def-sc-normalization] of the reduced irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family].

proof.text: Choose a perfect purely inseparable overfield $K/k$ using [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-purely-inseparable-overfield]. Index its finite intermediate extensions by inclusion. This is a nonempty directed set with union $K$: a finite family $a_1,\ldots,a_m$ lies in $k(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$, which is finite because each $a_j$ satisfies $T^{q^{n_j}}-a_j^{q^{n_j}}$ over $k$; the compositum of two such fields is generated by their two finite generating families. Every intermediate field is purely inseparable by the same power condition. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the inverse limit of their spectra. The same assertion for $X_K=\varprojlim X_{k_i}$ follows on every affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ from $A\otimes_kK=\varinjlim(A\otimes_kk_i)$; tensor generators and their bilinear relations give this colimit identity. Transition maps are affine since on these charts they are maps of spectra.

For each field $F$ occurring here, $X_F$ and its reduction are finite type over $F$: affine charts are generated by the images of the finitely many generators of the original chart, and taking the quotient by the nilradical preserves these generators. Fields are Noetherian (their ideals are $0$ and $1$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] gives Noetherianity, and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] gives quasi-separatedness. Normalize $(X_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$ componentwise and call the result $N_K$. The finite surjective map supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change], followed by reduction, is a finite surjective map $\nu_K:N_K\to X_K$: on an affine chart the reduction map is $A\to A/\sqrt0$, and a finite module over this quotient is also a finite module over $A$.

The scheme $N_K$ is normal, with no irreducibility assumption on $X$. On a reduced integral component $C$ of $X_K$, [def-sc-normalization] describes its normalization on each affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by the integral closure of $A$ in the function field of $C$. Apply [lem-sbc-integral-closure-finite-normal-product] with the one-element family consisting of that field: its prime localizations are integrally closed domains. [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] makes the component normalizations open and closed in $N_K$, so their local-ring assertion covers every point. Moreover $\nu_K$ is of finite presentation: each affine target ring $A$ is Noetherian, a finite $A$-module algebra is a finite type $A$-algebra, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] makes its relations finitely generated; the finite affine morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

Descend the finitely presented $X_K$-scheme $N_K$ along the system $S_i=X_{k_i}$. Use the finite chart/overlap datum of [def-nagata-relative-gluing-datum-descent], and its common equality stage [def-nagata-relative-gluing-valid-stage]. [lemma-nagata-relative-gluing-axioms-eventually] supplies the inverse and cocycle equations there, and [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] realizes the datum by an actual scheme, as required in [def-nagata-finite-presentation-descent]. Apply [lemma-nagata-finite-presentation-descends]: it gives a finitely presented morphism $\nu:Y\to X_{k_i}$ whose base change to $K$ is exactly $\nu_K$. The base stages are qcqs by step 2, the transitions are affine by step 1, and the morphism being descended is finitely presented by step 3. This invokes the existing descent construction and its property theorem, not merely a definition as a theorem of existence.

source.place: Tag 0BXT descent paragraph; Limits Tag 01ZM, label lemma-descend-finite-presentation, clause (1), realized by the existing Nagata construction

proof.text: Use the tail system $S_j=X_{k_j}$, $j\ge i$, with limit $X_K$, taking $Y$ and $X_{k_i}$ as the two schemes over $S_i$. After increasing $k_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite] makes $\nu$ finite. Its hypotheses hold: $X_{k_i}$ is qcqs by step 2, $Y$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] applied to its finitely presented structure morphism, and $\nu$ is locally of finite type because it is finitely presented. Finiteness persists at all later stages: affine coordinates become $B\otimes_{k_i}k_j$ over $A\otimes_{k_i}k_j$, generated as a module by the images of any finite set of $A$-module generators of $B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normality-perfect-closure-test] to $Y/k_i$: its base change is the normal $N_K$, and $K/k_i$ is perfect and purely inseparable since all the powers in step 1 already belong to $k\subseteq k_i$. Thus $Y$ is geometrically normal. The same test proves this again after any subsequent enlargement of $k_i$, since its base change to $K$ remains $N_K$.

source.place: Tag 0BXT geometric-normality and finiteness paragraphs; Limits Tag 01ZO, label lemma-descend-finite-finite-presentation; Varieties Tag 038O

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change], the normal locus of $(X_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is dense open and the normalization is an isomorphism over it. Let $V_K$ be the corresponding open of $X_K$, using the identical underlying space of reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Then $\nu_K^{-1}(V_K)\to V_K$ is a closed immersion with source $(V_K)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Its preimage is dense in $N_K$: each component normalization has the same function field as its reduced integral component by [def-sc-normalization], so its generic point lies above the generic point of that component, which belongs to the normal locus. Every component therefore meets the preimage. All these opens are quasi-compact, since the schemes are Noetherian by step 2 (for $N_K$ use its finite type over $K$, immediate from its finite map).

source.place: Tag 0BXT dense-open paragraph; Varieties Tag 0BXR and Morphisms Tag 035O

proof.text: Use [pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends] on the system $X_{k_j}$ to descend $V_K$ to a quasi-compact open $V\subset X_{k_i}$ after another enlargement. For closed-immersion descent take the tail system $S_j=\operatorname{Spec}k_j$ with limit $\operatorname{Spec}K$; the two schemes over its initial stage are $\nu^{-1}(V)$ and $V$. Restrict the descended finite map to $\nu^{-1}(V)\to V$ and apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion]. Its base change to $K$ is the closed immersion in step 6, it is locally of finite type (finite), and its source and target are qcqs: $Y$ is finite type over $k_i$, hence Noetherian, and inverse images of quasi-compact opens under the finite affine map are quasi-compact; they are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Enlarge once more to obtain a closed immersion on this open. The descended open is in $X_{k_i}$, correcting the source's typo $V\subset Y$.

source.place: Tag 0BXT open/closed-immersion descent paragraph (correct V subset X_{k_i}); Limits Tags 01Z4 and 01ZP

proof.text:
Set $k'=k_i$ at the final stage. Both $X_K	o X_{k'}$ and $N_K=Y_K	o Y$ are homeomorphisms by [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep], since $K/k'$ is purely inseparable. Write these homeomorphisms as $h_X:X_K	o X_{k'}$ and $h_Y:N_K	o Y$, so $h_X
u_K=
u h_Y$. For $x\in X_{k'}$, choose its preimage $x_K$ and then $y_K$ with $
u_K(y_K)=x_K$; then $
u(h_Y(y_K))=x$. Also $h_X^{-1}(V)=V_K$ and $h_Y^{-1}(
u^{-1}(V))=
u_K^{-1}(V_K)$. A homeomorphism identifies closures, so density of these two inverse images implies density of $V$ and $
u^{-1}(V)$. The closed immersion $
u^{-1}(V)	o V$ is surjective on points and its source is reduced, since $Y$ is normal (step 5): a nilpotent section has zero germ in every domain stalk and therefore is zero. Use the affine quotient characterization of [def-weil-closed-immersion]. On each affine open it is a quotient $A	woheadrightarrow B$ with radical kernel $I$ and $V(I)=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Thus $I=\sqrt0$, and $B=A/\sqrt0$. Consequently $
u^{-1}(V)\cong V_{\mathrm{red}}$ over $V$. This argument identifies the closed subscheme scheme-theoretically, rather than merely its image.

source.place: Tag 0BXT final paragraph; Picard-framework purely inseparable homeomorphism; closed subscheme/reduction definitions

proof.text: Let $N$ be the componentwise normalization of $(X_{k'})_{\mathrm{red}}$. It is finite over $X_{k'}$ by the same quotient-ring argument as in step 2, and normal by the componentwise application of [lem-sbc-integral-closure-finite-normal-product] in step 3. The open $V_{\mathrm{red}}$ is normal because it is isomorphic to the open $\nu^{-1}(V)$ of the normal $Y$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change] identifies $N|_V$ with $V_{\mathrm{red}}$. Its preimage is dense in $N$, since $V$ is dense in the Noetherian target and contains every component generic point, and the component normalization has the same function field [def-sc-normalization]. Both finite normal sources $N$ and $Y$ thus have dense inverse images of $V$ and an isomorphism there over $X_{k'}$. Apply [lem-sbc-finite-normal-dense-open-iso] with locally Noetherian base $X_{k'}$ to obtain $N\cong Y$ over $X_{k'}$. For each field extension $L/k'$, this isomorphism base changes to $N_L\cong Y_L$; the latter has normal local rings by step 5. This proves every clause, with $k'/k$ finite purely inseparable by step 1.
